paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Pride tells you that you're up too high for anything to reach you. Edom said in its heart, "Who can bring me down to the ground?" (Obadiah 1:3), and the LORD answered, "even from there I will bring you down" (Obadiah 1:4). Nobody is on a shelf too high for God, and that includes me and you.

The LORD also tells us what Edom did wrong, and it wasn't only what Edom did with its hands. Edom stood aloof while strangers carried off its brother's wealth, and the LORD says, "you were just like one of them" (Obadiah 1:11). Standing there doing nothing while your family hurts is NOT neutral. Then comes the line that should make us all stop: "As you have done, it will be done to you" (Obadiah 1:15). So when somebody else is having their worst day, we don't gloat, we don't cheer, and we don't walk away.

Now here's the good news, and I LOVE this part. Edom's story ends in stubble, but God's people don't end there, because "on Mount Zion there will be deliverance, and it will be holy" (Obadiah 1:17). The very last words say it all: "the kingdom will belong to the LORD" (Obadiah 1:21). That's why I keep my ovens ready, baker. Every high place gets measured against His kingdom, so don't build your nest among the stars, and stay close to the One who holds it all.
